newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ARCON plans new company for hydrocarbon unit.
newsitem.headline: ARCON plans new company for hydrocarbon unit.

text.p: ARCON International Resources Plc said on Monday that it plans to transfer its hydrocarbon interests into a separate company which would be quoted on the Exploration Securities Market of the Irish Stock Exchange.

The move will allow ARCON to focus on and develop its mining activities and mineral exploration, the company said in a statement. It will also pursue expansion through acquisition of mining and mineral exploration targets.
ARCON shareholders will receive one share in the new company, Providence Resources Plc, for every one share held in ARCON.
ARCON's hydrocarbon division comprises the assets and liabilities of its hydrocarbon business and has a book value of 6.55 million Irish pounds.

"It's a win-win situation for our shareholders. ARCON benefits from a more focused corporate mission with lower operating costs at a time of rising zinc prices and a successful exploration programme," ARCON chief executive Tony O'Reilly Junior said.
"Shareholders will have the opportunity to hold an investment in ARCON and also in a hydrocarbon business which has considerable potential," he said.
ARCON said the impact of the demerger would be cash positive for ARCON.
It said the separation of the hydrocarbon interests was part of an ongoing programme of restructuring taking place that should deliver better returns for shareholders.

"Having now successfully established concentrate production and sales, ARCON is currently arranging more favourable banking and financing facilities which, when added to ARCON's cashflow from its mining activities, will provide funding for a vigorous acquisition and exploration programme in the mining sector," ARCON said.
It added that no rights issue is presently envisaged or required by ARCON.
